entities.summary: Bakur III, the last Chosroid king of Iberia, played a pivotal role in the downfall of the Iberian monarchy. His reign, spanning from approximately 570 to 580 CE, was marked by the increasing influence of Sassanid Iran, which eventually led to the abolition of the Iberian monarchy. This event had far-reaching consequences, as it marked the end of a centuries-old dynasty and the beginning of a new era of Iranian dominance in the region. The legacy of Bakur III continues to be felt in the modern-day cultural and historical heritage of the region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bakur III's reign marked the beginning of the end of the Iberian monarchy, which had a lasting impact on the region's politics and culture. The event had significant consequences, including the incorporation of the Iberian Kingdom into the Sassanid Empire and the rise of Iranian dominance in the region.
